key_insight: For LPBF A20X alloy, friction stir welding alone preserved better corrosion resistance than post-weld solution treatment and aging, which increased corrosion susceptibility.
engineering_relevance: For aerospace joining of LPBF parts, welding and heat-treatment schedules must be co-optimized because post-weld aging can negate corrosion performance gains.
method: Compared four conditions: base material, as-welded stir zone, peak-aged base material, and peak-aged stir zone.
Used electron microscopy and XRD to track microstructural changes after FSW and heat treatment.
Evaluated corrosion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and potentiodynamic polarization.
evidence_signal: The lowest corrosion current density was measured for BM (0.703 µA/cm²), while SZ, BM–PA, and SZ–PA were progressively higher at 0.966, 2.257, and 3.181 µA/cm², respectively.
watch_item: The study suggests a possible micro-galvanic role from Cu-rich constituents, TiB2 particles, and the Al matrix, but the mechanism remains inferential and should be validated for broader processing windows.
paper_title: Influence of Friction Stir Welding and Post-Weld Aging on Corrosion Behavior of LPBF A20X Alloy
